title: The first nun
hookLine: Mahapajapati, who raised the Buddha, opens the way for women to go forth, then asks him for a short teaching she can take away and practice (Vinaya, Cullavagga 10; AN 8.53)

lines: THE LONG WALK, IN YEAR ONE.
cards: She has already done the hard part.

In our first year we watched Mahapajapati, the aunt who raised the Buddha after his mother died, walk to Vesali with the Sakyan women, feet swollen, covered in dust, to ask that women be allowed to go forth.
We heard Ananda speak for her, and the answer finally become yes. In the Vinaya, she is the first woman to receive ordination. So what does someone do after she's changed everything?
Mahapajapati goes back to her teacher, and asks him for something small.

teach.b: First, her request. In the Anguttara Nikaya, Mahapajapati asks the Buddha for a teaching in brief, so that she can go off alone and practice it, diligent and resolute.
Not a title, not a place of honor: a short teaching she can carry. Second, the answer is a test.

Gotami, he says, using her clan name, whatever things you know lead to dispassion, not passion; to release, not bondage; to letting go, not piling up; to few wants, not many; to contentment, not discontent; to solitude, not company; to energy, not laziness; to being easy to support, not burdensome: know for certain that this is the teaching, this is the discipline.
Eight tests, each with its opposite. He doesn't hand her a list of beliefs; he hands her a way to check anything. A tool, not a fence.
And few wants and contentment may sound familiar from Anuruddha's grove four days ago. Third, her title.
The same Anguttara list of outstanding disciples names her foremost among the nuns of long standing, the senior one. She went first, and she stayed. Fourth, her own words.

teach.h: HER THANKS, IN HER OWN VERSES.
teach.b: Her verses survive in the Therigatha, the poems of the elder nuns.
In them she gives thanks to the Buddha, and says that through him she was freed from much suffering. The woman who raised him calls him the one who set her free.

how: Mahapajapati Gotami is honored in Buddhist traditions as the founder of the order of nuns, and her brief teaching's eight tests are taught as a way to recognize the Dhamma in any instruction.

o: a woman who serves monks their food
a laywoman who keeps eight precepts

dispassion, release, few wants, and more
foremost among nuns of long standing

s: after the women were admitted, Mahapajapati asked for a position of honor

games.q: you're Mahapajapati. women can now go forth, and you were the first. what do you ask the Buddha for next?
o: a place of honor for the nuns.
a short teaching to practice alone.
games.why: she asks for a teaching in brief, and he gives her eight tests to tell what leads to freedom from what doesn't.

practice: Bring to mind a woman who opened a door you later walked through: a grandmother who left a village, a teacher who was the only woman in the room, the first in your family to go to school, to speak up, to leave.
You may know her name, or only her story. If you pray, remember her in your own way; if you don't, simply keep her company for a minute, the way the Therigatha keeps these women's voices.

wordCard.voice: Bhikkhuni, a fully ordained nun. What Mahapajapati became first, after opening the way for women to go forth. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali bhikkhuni: a fully ordained nun. Mahapajapati was the first, in the Vinaya's account.

carryVoice: Your line: she went first. And then she looked back and said thank you. That's day seven hundred fifty-three.
